items.question: What column layout and header names does the CSV use?
items.chose: Writes the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created' with the columns in that order.
items.instead: Use raw field names such as id,title,status,openings,filled,createdAt, or a different column order.

items.question: Does the CSV start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.chose: Prepends a BOM (U+FEFF) to the output.
items.instead: Emit plain CSV with no BOM.

items.question: Which line terminator is used, and does the last row end with one?
items.chose: Ends every line, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Join lines with LF, or with no trailing newline after the last row.

items.question: What does an empty requisition list produce?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header line only.
items.instead: Return an empty string, or throw.

items.question: In what order do the rows appear?
items.chose: Sorts a copy by createdAt ascending, then by id in code-unit order.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC string from toISOString(), including milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date-only value (YYYY-MM-DD) or a locale-formatted date.

items.question: How is a missing or null title written?
items.instead: Write the text 'null' or 'undefined', or throw.

items.question: How are fields that contain commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Quotes the field per RFC 4180 and doubles any embedded quotes. Embedded newlines stay inside the quotes.
items.instead: Quote every field, or strip or replace the special characters.

items.question: Are values that start with =, +, - or @ neutralised against spreadsheet formula injection?
items.chose: Does nothing. Titles and ids that start with those characters are written as they are.
items.instead: Prefix such values with a single quote or a tab.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an unknown status?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id, for any status outside open, on_hold, filled and cancelled.
items.instead: Write the status through unchanged, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when openings or filled is negative, fractional, NaN, infinite or not a number?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id and the bad field. Zero is accepted.
items.instead: Clamp or coerce the value, or skip the row.

items.question: What happens when filled is greater than openings, or the creation time is an invalid date? Does one bad row fail the whole export?
items.chose: Validates every row before building anything, and throws on the first bad one, which rejects the whole export.
items.instead: Skip the bad rows and export the rest, or write them with a flag column.
